Cybersecurity and Operational Resilience
Operational risk remained a key focus area in 2025,
with cyber threats and fraud attempts increasing
across the financial services sector. Stanbic
responded by strengthening its cybersecurity and
operational‑resilience capabilities across multiple
layers of defence.
The Group operates a fully integrated Group
Security Operations Centre (SOC), supported by
country‑level teams, enabling continuous monitoring
and rapid response to cyber threats. In parallel,
the implementation of a new fraud‑management
solution delivered a material reduction in fraud losses,
(provide metrics to support this narrative) while
machine‑learning‑based detection tools enhanced the
Group’s ability to identify anomalous behaviour in real
time. What was the detection rate?
Recognising that cyber risk extends beyond technology,
the Group also intensified customer‑protection
initiatives, including targeted education and enhanced
transaction controls. Social‑engineering attacks
remained a key risk vector, reinforcing the importance of
behavioural awareness alongside technical safeguards.
Cyber and fraud risks form part of the seventeen
operational‑risk categories monitored against defined
thresholds.
Predictive Fraud Capability
In support of a rapidly digitising operating model, the
Group continued to embed predictive‑risk controls
across high‑volume processes. The deployment of
automation and robotics process automation (RPA)
reduced manual intervention, lowered error rates and
strengthened control environments in mission‑critical
operations.
Straight‑through processing for domestic and
cross‑border payments, coupled with enhanced digital
onboarding and automated (Know Your Customer)
reviews, further reduced operational risks and
strengthened financial‑crime controls. These capabilities
not only improved efficiency and customer experience
but also enhanced the Group’s ability to detect and
prevent fraudulent activities at scale.
